name: Francium
occurrence: The rarest naturally occurring element after astatine — at any moment, less than an ounce is estimated to exist across the entire Earth's crust, from radioactive decay.
majorUses: No practical applications — studied only for fundamental atomic physics research due to its extreme scarcity and radioactivity
safetyNotes: Intensely radioactive with a longest half-life of just 22 minutes, making it far too unstable to ever accumulate or handle in bulk.
notableCharacteristics: The most electropositive and, alongside caesium, one of the most reactive elements ever isolated — theoretically the most reactive alkali metal, though its radioactivity prevents it from ever being studied in bulk quantity.
ncertRelevance: extreme reactivity of Group 1 at the bottom of the table
whyHere: Sitting at the very bottom of Group 1, francium's single 7s electron is held more loosely by the nucleus than in any other stable or semi-stable alkali metal, which would in theory make it the most reactive of all — if it lasted long enough to react with anything before decaying.
didYouKnow: Francium was discovered by Marguerite Perey while she was reanalyzing what her lab believed was an impure sample of actinium — she correctly identified a genuinely new, previously unknown decay product instead.
genZNote: Theoretically the most reactive alkali metal ever, but decays too fast to actually prove it. All hype, no time.
